core_obligations: Consider the kernel ideal I of O_Y -> f_*O_X and note that the closed subscheme it defines works when I is quasi-coherent (proof lines 3211-3215).
In general apply the existence of a largest quasi-coherent subsheaf to obtain I' contained in I (proof lines 3216-3219).
Conclude that the closed subspace defined by I' factors f and is contained in every closed subspace through which f factors (proof lines 3206-3208).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma, opening with the slogan that the scheme-theoretic image exists: for a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S there is a closed subspace Z through which f factors and which is contained in every other closed subspace with that property (source lines 3200-3209). The proof takes the kernel ideal of O_Y -> f_*O_X, notes that if it were quasi-coherent the closed subscheme it defines would do, and then invokes the existence of the largest quasi-coherent subsheaf of a given submodule to produce the required ideal in general.
